geo_basis: Bulgarian government (Sofia); the affected agencies are not named
title: Bulgaria says hackers had access to government networks for about five years
date_note: Date of the government announcement; the access began in 2021.
summary: Bulgaria's digital minister Ivan Vasilev said hackers had unauthorised access to state networks from 2021 and took at least 130 GB of documents, over 62 million pages. A new national monitoring system exposed the intrusion. He said access was cut and malware removed, and that no evidence shows citizens' personal data was taken. The file went to prosecutors; the attackers are unidentified.
plain: Bulgaria says unidentified hackers sat inside government networks for about five years and copied a very large volume of state documents. Access has been cut off.
exec: A multi-year, undetected intrusion into a national government shows how long attackers can stay hidden without central monitoring.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Government and critical-sector defenders should review document-exchange systems for long-dwell access and centralise monitoring.

validation.note: Two independent publishers (Samanyolu Haber, citing DW Türkçe; Europa FM, citing Novinite) report the minister's announcement. Detection date differs (June 23 vs August 2026) and Europa FM gives the volume in gigabits; the DW-based report says GB, so GB is used. The DW original and a government statement were not read.

review.note: Compared with Samanyolu Haber and Europa FM: minister Vasilev, from 2021, 130 GB/62M pages, no personal data evidence, access cut, attackers unidentified; detection date discrepancy already noted
